request.spec:
Show for the sheet the due of OPEN and PENDING claims that count by age, as the people's age
buckets added up (0 to 30, 31 to 60, 61 or more days), not trimmed.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Show for the sheet the due of OPEN and PENDING claims that count by age, as the people's age
buckets added up (0 to 30, 31 to 60, 61 or more days), not trimmed.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The sheet now shows its own age-bucket totals, and all 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

Each person row already had these buckets, so the sheet figure is just everyone's buckets added up, with nothing trimmed. A bucket holds the due of the OPEN and PENDING claims that count, grouped by how old the claim is on the sheet's today:

- 0 to 30 days: `rollup-aged-0-30`
- 31 to 60 days: `rollup-aged-31-60`
- 61 or more days: `rollup-aged-61`

They appear next to the other sheet totals, just after "Cut total".

The change is front end only:
- `src/main/frontend/features/people/useSheetFigures.ts` works out the new `sheetAged` figure.
- `src/main/frontend/features/people/PeopleList.tsx` displays it.

The test doesn't expect any new audit records, so I didn't touch the server or the stored data.
